title: Pinned real Ribasim two-recipient priority-conflict bridge
purpose: Reproduce the DUMMY-15 same-source competing-claims priority split in the pinned real Ribasim allocator while deliberately disabling physical UserDemand reduction as a confounding mechanism.

basin.physical_reduction_control: storage remains far above Ribasim low-storage threshold

level_hold.meaning: highest-priority storage objective forces zero Basin storage change, so UserDemand allocation is limited by the 32 m3/day inflow rather than initial Basin storage

model.physical_control: Basin level is held at 1 m and both UserDemand min_level values are 0 m, so source low-storage/min-level reduction factors must remain effectively 1; D19B tests allocation priority, not physical curtailment.

authority_basis.priority_order: Pinned Ribasim get_all_demand_priorities sorts priorities ascending; allocation objectives are executed lexicographically and earlier optimums are constrained before later objectives.
authority_basis.observability: Qualified DUMMY-19A binds demand, allocated and physical supplied/linkflow observability and one-record supplied-output lag.
authority_basis.supply_measurement: Use direct Basin->UserDemand physical link flows as primary supplied authority; allocation result supplied may be used only with D19A-qualified lag alignment.

hypotheses: Both pinned real Ribasim models execute successfully.
ROOT_FIRST real allocation supplies 32 m3/day to root proxy and 0 to external demand.
EXTERNAL_FIRST real allocation supplies 20 m3/day to external demand and 12 m3/day to root proxy.
In both cases the sum of allocated UserDemand is 32 m3/day and no UserDemand allocation exceeds its demand.
Direct physical Basin->UserDemand linkflow matches allocated flow because low-storage and min-level reduction are inactive by construction.
The Basin remains at 1 m within numerical tolerance, demonstrating that the scarcity is the 32 m3/day source inflow rather than depletion of initial storage.
Priority reversal changes recipient split but not total supplied managed water or Basin physical trajectory, matching the structural DUMMY-15 invariant.
D19B establishes only the same-state allocation-priority bridge; it does not yet test allocation-versus-physical-realization conflict.
forbidden: no modification of pinned Ribasim source
no use of initial Basin storage as hidden extra supply
no physical min-level reduction in this work unit
no claim that this one-Basin model represents full Ribasim network allocation
no tuning after observing D19B results
